narrative:
The model estimates a 73% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your professional background that, according to patterns seen across many similar employees, strongly signal a higher likelihood of departure.

Your total years of experience (6–10 years) was the single most influential factor. While many employees predicted to stay have either very short (1–5 years) or much longer careers, your mid-range experience level pushed the prediction toward leaving. Similarly, the time you have spent in your current organization (1–5 years) was the second strongest driver; this relatively short tenure in your present role also pulled the outcome toward departure, as longer stays in one workplace are more common among those expected to remain.

The third major influence was that you have received other job offers while working here. Having external opportunities consistently increases the chance an employee will leave, and your situation follows that pattern.

Taken together, these three factors outweighed positive elements such as your medical-sector role, received bonus, useful training, and high emotional commitment. The organization should discuss retention strategies with you, such as clearer promotion paths or adjusted responsibilities, while you may wish to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your longer-term goals.
